_comment: Service configuration. Copy to service.json and edit; service.json is
gitignored so a real allowlist and a real bot account never land in git.
bot.account   the GitHub account the bot posts as. Swappable: nothing in
the code names it. Start with a throwaway account, move to a
real one by editing this file.
bot.token_env the environment variable holding its token. The token itself
is never in this file, and never on a bench machine.
allowlist     who may trigger a run (role: user). A run costs ~1h of
exclusive machine time and executes PR compiler code, so
this is a privilege. Extend it by editing this file -- no
deploy needed.
admins        the privileged subset: may use force=true and priority=top,
cancel anyone's run, and operate machines. An admin does not
also need to be in allowlist.
allow_associations  escape hatch, e.g. ["OWNER"]. Empty by default:
explicit logins beat inferred permissions.
machines      the slot registry. One entry = one concurrent run, because
the opam root lock is what serialises runs. No ssh entries
and no paths: the server never connects to a bench machine
(the agent dials out), and where things live on the machine
is the agent's own configuration. Names and policy only.
compiler_repo the clone URL that vs= versions/branches resolve against
(release tags, branch heads); PR heads resolve against the
PR's own repository.
Build flavors: the vs= `+name` suffixes (vs=5.5.0,5.5.0+fp).
A flavor is a named, allowlisted configure-time variant; adding
one is an edit here, not a deploy. List order is canonical (it
fixes runtime names like ocaml-5.5.0-fp-flambda); names and
configure_args must both be unique. Omit the key entirely for
the defaults, which are exactly these two.
flavors.name: fp

_comment: The execution timeout the agent enforces per run:
max(floor_seconds, multiplier * estimate). multiplier 0 (the
default) disables the deadline: until a machine has an established
result set the estimate is a guess, and a wedged run is still
killable via /bench cancel. Opt in once timings are trustworthy.
Verdict bands and gates for report.md (lib/report.ml). Provisional
until repeat-run noise data (Q12). wall/instructions/max RSS are
reported individually; wall needs wall_min_invocations for a verdict,
RSS needs the band AND rss_floor_kib moved.
